item.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
item.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. He said relations were strengthened by engagement between Angolan President João Lourenço and Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Zau said the Caculo Cabaça Dam would become operational in June 2027, with the capacity to generate at least 2,172 megawatts (MW). He said the dam would raise Angola’s total capacity from 6,400 MW to about 8,600 MW. He also highlighted the country’s achievements in 2026. (NAN) The post Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said diplomacy should resume “without further delay” to end the US-Iran war after talks with his Iranian counterpart. Erdogan met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN climate conference in the Turkish province of Antalya, his office said. During their discussion, Erdogan underscored “the importance of getting to the negotiating table without further delay” and said Turkey would continue to support efforts aimed at securing peace. “Common ground for agreement must be strengthened and diplomacy given a chance,” he said, expressing hope that the conflict with the US “would end as soon as possible”. The Middle East war broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian leaves after delivering a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP In an address to the UN climate summit on Wednesday, Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of inflicting severe environmental damage during attacks on the Islamic Republic. “The recent criminal and illegal aggression against Iran by America and the Zionist regime… has inflicted severe damage on the environment, releasing massive quantities of pollutants and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere,” he said. Diplomatic efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan have sought to negotiate an end to the war. Tehran wants Washington to accept a raft of demands including unfreezing assets and lifting sanctions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy conduit it has blockaded since the start of the conflict. AFP The post Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict appeared first on Channels Television .

The ruling followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the committee assumed leadership after the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. The court’s decision was reported to have affected the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate, as the Mark-led committee organised the primary election. The ADC, however, rejected the judgment, describing it as legally indefensible and accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of seeking to weaken the opposition. The party also said it would challenge the decision, citing an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, which it said had affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-led leadership. Speaking further on ADC’s standpoint on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Kola Ologbondiyan, Spokesperson of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of working toward coronating Tinubu in 2027 instead of allowing for healthy competition. item.title: Floyd Mayweather To Launch Tmt Frontrow Fight Series In Nigeria
item.description: ABUJA, NIGERIA – 11 November 2026 – Boxing legend Floyd “Money” Mayweather will arrive in Abuja on Thursday, 12 November, to announce the launch of the TMT Frontrow Fight Series Nigeria and explore investment opportunities in Nigeria’s mining and solid minerals sector. The initiative aims to identify, train and promote young Nigerian boxing talent through the Frontrow Fight Series boxing academies and grassroots development programmes across Lagos, Abuja, Enugu, Calabar and other locations. The first TMT Frontrow Fight Series event is planned for 2027, with Floyd Mayweather also fighting in Nigeria during the same year. ABUJA PRESS CONFERENCE Mayweather will address the media in Abuja on Friday, 13 November 2026, to outline the Frontrow Fight Series and its plans to develop and empower Nigerian youth through boxing. BANGKOK FIGHT – 19 DECEMBER 2026 Mayweather will also discuss his upcoming fight in Bangkok, Thailand, against Australian light heavyweight boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd, who has a professional record of 15 wins from 17 fights. Further details of the fight, including how Nigerian boxing fans can subscribe to watch the event, will be announced at the Abuja press conference. ABOUT TMT AFRICA & FRONTROW FIGHT SERIES TMT Africa and Frontrow Fight Series aims to develop Nigerian boxing talent and empower youths across Africa. It’s time to bring the benefit of Frontrow Fight Series to the Motherland and produce outstanding champions from the pool of untapped talent in Africa. item.title: Travelling to the UAE from Nigeria in 2027? Here’s What You Should Know About Tourist Visas Before You Fly
item.description: Planning a trip to Dubai in 2027? You are not alone. Every year, more and more travellers add the UAE to their holiday list. Some go for the beaches, some for the shopping, and others just want to see the famous Burj Khalifa up close. But before you book your flight, there is one important thing to take care of first, your visa. The good news is that getting a UAE tourist visa is easier than it used to be. Most of the process happens online, and your visa comes straight to your email. Still, the rules are not the same for every traveller. Some people get a visa on arrival, while others must apply before they fly. A few small mistakes can also slow things down or even get your application rejected. So let us walk through what you really need to know before you pack your bags. Do Nigerian Travellers Need a Visa for the UAE? Yes, Nigerian travellers need a visa to enter the United Arab Emirates for tourism. The UAE lets travellers from some countries enter without a visa, or get one when they land. But Nigeria is not on that list. If you hold a Nigerian passport, you must apply for your UAE tourist visa before you fly. That means you cannot just show up at Dubai International Airport and sort things out there. Your visa must be approved and in your inbox before you check in for your flight. The process is not hard, though. With the right documents and a trusted service, most people get through it without any stress. Whether this is your first trip or your fifth, this guide will help you from start to finish. UAE Tourist Visa Types: Picking the Right One for Your Trip The UAE offers a few tourist visa options. Some let you enter only once. Others let you come and go many times. The validity period also changes from one visa to another. For example, a visa might be valid for 60 days, but it may only let you stay for 30 days inside the country. Always read the details before you book your flight. item.title: Indonesian Vice President Resigns In High School Diploma Scandal
item.description: Indonesia’s vice president resigned Thursday, undone by a scandal over his high school diploma that has added to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires. There had been repeated calls for Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, to step down following a Supreme Court ruling last month to annul his high school qualification, obtained abroad. On Thursday, he submitted his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto and to parliament. Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka (C) arrives at the vice president’s palace after submitting his resignation letter to the People’s Consultative Assembly in Jakarta on November 12, 2026. Photo by ABIMANYU / AFP Prabowo told reporters he had accepted Gibran’s resignation “with a heavy heart” and praised him for acting “for a greater cause, for the interests of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia”. “He certainly feels that he has pursued his education through an orderly process, but we all understand that the education system abroad is different from the education system in Indonesia,” the president said. Indonesia’s vice president does not have many constitutionally defined powers apart from acting as the president’s representative at official events and taking over if his boss is incapacitated. ‘Political realignment’ Gibran’s downfall came after thousands of Indonesians took to the streets in recent weeks to protest economic hardship, graft, perceived authoritarianism and the government’s handling of months of devastating wildfires emitting toxic haze. University students protest demanding a government review including lowering the prices of basic commodities, military involvement in civilian affairs, free meal program, taxation of sanitary pads and addressing the issue of wildfires in Surabaya on November 10, 2026. (Photo by Juni KRISWANTO / AFP) | Juni KRISWANTO / AFP His exit is likely to complicate a loose governing alliance that includes the parties of Prabowo and of his predecessor Joko Widodo — Gibran’s father, who goes by Jokowi. The resignation “marks a significant political realignment, but does not necessarily threaten government stability”, according to Khairul Fahmi, executive director of the Institute for Security and Strategic Studies (ISESS) think tank. “Jokowi will retain political influence, but Gibran’s departure could reduce his network’s direct access to power. For Prabowo, this creates greater room to consolidate his leadership and pursue his own political agenda,” Khairul told AFP. Two years into his term, Prabowo’s popularity has reached record lows. Last week, Indonesian authorities arrested the former national police chief and three senior police officials for allegedly tapping the president’s telephone. On Thursday, police said they were investigating possible treason. Prabowo’s rise to power was widely credited to support from the popular Jokowi, who served two terms from 2014 to 2024. item.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: US media
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang — to whom he bears no familial relation — in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement. He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair. item.title: COP31: UK Makes History, Appoints World’s First ‘Climate Security’ Envoy
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced on Thursday the appointment of a special envoy focused on “climate security”, a world first, to better prepare for the growing impacts of global warming. In a speech to the UN’s COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, the Labour leader recalled that he spent his first three weeks as prime minister this past summer responding to the worst wildfires Britain ever experienced. “I decided then it was important for me to be here to show British leadership in a world where climate issues have taken too much of a backseat,” said Burnham, who was the only G7 leader attending the summit. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres delivers a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Britain and the rest of western Europe experienced their hottest summer on record, with a succession of heatwaves and wildfires. The heat caused tens of thousands of excess deaths on the continent. “Climate is a national security issue,” Burnham said. “As evidence of that, I am today announcing the appointment of Dame Madeleine Alessandri as the first UK special representative for climate security,” he said. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Alessandri is the former head of the UK’s Joint Intelligence Committee, the body that briefs ministers on security threats. “In this role, I will work with partners across government and internationally to strengthen our understanding of climate threats, build resilience, and ensure we are better prepared for the challenges ahead,” Alessandri said in a statement. Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva delivers a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP Britain has a climate minister, Katie White, who is in Antalya for the COP31 talks that are scheduled to end on November 20. Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think-tank E3G, said countries often have climate envoys and climate security is part of their remit. “This is the first climate security envoy specifically,” she told AFP. “This appointment elevates that issue to the level it deserves, and other governments should consider a similar model,” Cassel said. Environmental group Greenpeace also said the appointment was a “welcome move” as climate change is a “threat multiplier”. item.title: Court orders extradition of Nigerian to US over alleged wire fraud, others
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the extradition of a Nigerian, Temitope Omotade, to the U.S. District Court of Minnesota to face his trial over allegations bordering on wire fraud, among others. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgment, held that the application made by the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) was meritorious. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the AGF had made the application for the extradition of Omotade to the U.S. He is a suspect in a superseding five-count indictment bordering on five counts in case number 22-CR-24 SRN/HB filed on Feb. 8, 2022, at the US District Court. The offences in counts one, two and three bordered on mail and wire fraud in violation of Title 18 US Code, Sections 1341 and 1343, and 1349, which carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison in each of the counts. Counts four and five bordered on aggravated identity theft and aiding and abetting, in violation of Title 18 US Codes, Sections 1028A (a)(1) and 2, which carries a maximum penalty of two years in prison for each count, consecutive to any other term of imprisonment imposed on the defendant. In the AGF’s application, he contended that the request was grounded on an extradition packet and diplomatic notes from the US, including a sealed indictment from the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota and a warrant for Omotade’s arrest. He argued that all statutory requirements under the Extradition Act have been met because the offences are non-political, non-trivial, and made in good faith. He submitted that the Central Authority Unit had established that proper certifications and documentation, including affidavits from US officials, relevant statute copies, and passport details, accompanied the formal request. Besides, the AGF said there were no pending local criminal proceedings in Nigeria against Omotade for the specified offences, and adequate assurances regarding nonprejudicial trial conditions in the US had been secured. He asserted that the request and accompanying materials satisfied all conditions for the surrender of Omotade, who was the sole respondent in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/494/2024. The AGF maintained that the legal procedures complied with the Oaths Act and the Extradition Act, adding that the interest of justice dictated that the request be granted, “as the respondent is duly accused of the indictments brought against him abroad.” But Omotade, in his counter-affidavit filed by his lawyer, prayed the court to dismiss the suit. Omotade denied all allegations of mail fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft, maintaining that his connection to Roxanne Gilbert involved no criminal conduct or digital proceeds. He contended that the extradition application lacked substantive proof and statutory backing for several reasons. item.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
item.description: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage. With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington. The 80-year-old Republican heads to the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate. Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage. “After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing. – Iran, trade, China – That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics. China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations. “In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month. “The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.” Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia. Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports. Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy. The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump’s policies, though. The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use. – High-profile meeting – Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. item.title: Two Dead, Several Injured As New York Building Collapses
item.description: Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said. Images from the scene showed firefighters sifting through a pile of rubble in front of what appeared to be a residential property with its walls torn down, exposing a bedroom and a clothing wardrobe. The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people whom firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws. “We do not know how many people are still in the collapse zone, and this will be a prolonged operation,” FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore told reporters at the scene in Flatbush, Brooklyn late Wednesday. First responders tend to a collapsed building in Brooklyn in New York on November 11, 2026. She said two people had died, without disclosing their ages, and said 17 others were hurt, including seven children. Four people were critically injured. More than 250 firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene, the FDNY wrote on X, adding that the cause of the collapse was under investigation. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani praised the emergency services for their work, saying the site involved “precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface.” “I want to ask New Yorkers to please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss,” he added at a news conference. New York Fire Department Chief John Esposito speaks next to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a press conference after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on November 11, 2026. One witness, named only as Anthony, told PIX11 News that he heard people screaming and a “bomb”-like noise as the building collapsed. Another witness, Melissa Orna, told The New York Times: “The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell.” The city’s Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene “assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings.” Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of the department, said construction workers were performing excavation at the time of the collapse. He added that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building. item.title: Who could potentially replace Jensen Huang if Nvidia ousts him?
item.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to US media. The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered with reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data center executive who has been accused by US intelligence of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. With Huang unexpectedly on the backfoot, and no known plan of succession at Nvidia, the field is wide open for a variety of replacements to lead one of the key AI players should the board decide to oust Huang. Here are some of the names being suggested most frequently as Huang’s potential successor. Internal hire With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports. Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth. Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data center clients. He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand. Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick. A family affair Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession. His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts. As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH. Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor. He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division. Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection – not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD. Tech CEO swap Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang. Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press. Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped. item.title: Trump Defends Iran War In Veterans Day Address
item.description: President Donald Trump defended the war against Iran Wednesday at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defense secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum. “The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington. “When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer.” U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP The war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 US service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979.” U.S. President Donald Trump and U.S. Vice President JD Vance participate in a wreath-laying ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2025 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP He stressed that US forces were acting to halt Iran’s capacity to build a nuclear weapon. Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America’s lost service members. During his speech before troops, veterans and top officials in his administration, Trump namechecked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was in attendance, saying he had “done a fantastic job.” Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort — launched by an outgoing Republican lawmaker — to impeach Hegseth for allegedly waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. item.title: Student Loan: Parents, NANS offer tips on how to stop double dipping by beneficiaries
item.description: By Adesina Wahab Parents under the aegis of National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, and the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, have offered tips on how to stop the practice of students benefitting from the Student Loan Scheme and still going ahead to collect tuition fees from their parents and guardians. The practice, labelled double dipping by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, which gives out the loans, is gradually becoming rampant and erasing the main reason the loan scheme was initiated – take the burden of tuition payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Speaking with Thursday Learning, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Deolu Ogunbanjo, opined that such a practice negates the reason for the setting up of the scheme. “The Student Loan Scheme was set up to give access to higher education to students who would otherwise drop out because of inability to pay fees. It is also to take the burden of fee payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Such happenings may not be totally eradicated. We know how rascally some young ones can be. “I think the way out is to let the parents and guardians be aware when payments are made by NELFUND to beneficiaries. Let there be a means of notifying the parents that their children have benefitted from the scheme,” he said Similarly, the National Public Relations Officer of NANS, Comrade Obidah David, also supported notification being sent to parents of beneficiaries. “If it is a text message, they can send to parents and guardians of beneficiaries. Information on contacts of parents is always provided by students when registering. That is necessary in case of any emergency. Also, names of beneficiaries can be published whether in the traditional media or social media. There is nothing bad in that. It is for transparency, “ he stated. Recall that recently, the Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, said during a press briefing that the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. They are taking from NELFUND and still stressing their parents. We are going to put an end to that,” he said. Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. Sawyerr said the initiative was intended to address concerns among parents who continued to shoulder the financial responsibilities of their children’s education despite the availability of government-backed loans. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 12, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, maintaining the wider spread observed earlier in the week. At the official window, data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the naira entering Thursday’s session around the ₦1,350.36 to ₦1,353.50 per dollar band. Early Thursday morning international currency feeds recorded spot quotes hovering near ₦1,345.72 per dollar, while official NFEM benchmarks reflect the closing figures from the prior trading session pending the day’s official fixing. Earlier in the week, trading at the official window saw intraday fluctuations between ₦1,349.25 and ₦1,354 per dollar, with interbank turnover reaching $248.07 million across 144 deals. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a significant discount to the official rate. Currency dealers across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,411 and ₦1,420 for buying, while selling rates ranged from ₦1,419 to ₦1,430 per dollar depending on transaction volume and location. This leaves an exchange rate gap of roughly ₦68 to ₦80 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and street-level rates. Market analysts attribute the recent softening of the local currency to heightened seasonal foreign exchange demand from importers and travelers heading into the end-of-year period, alongside foreign portfolio investment outflows and a firmer US dollar globally. Despite the recent dip—which saw the parallel market touch a 10-month low of ₦1,430 per dollar this week—Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain sturdy at approximately $54.9 billion, well above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion, offering a substantial buffer to support market liquidity through the remainder of the fourth quarter. Traders and businesses continue to monitor daily NFEM liquidity injections and CBN updates for direction as Thursday’s trading progresses. item.title: My research effective for prostate, menopause therapy — Odimegwu, Gates Foundation Scholar
item.description: By Morenike Taire Joy Odimegwu, a University of Lagos academic in the Department of Pharmacognosy, Faculty of Pharmacy, is a senior researcher with over 20 years of international experience with a passion for translating herbal medicine drug discovery from labs to markets to solve some of the world’s most pressing health care challenges, including drug resistant gynecological cancers and pain. As a fellow of Mujeres Por Africa and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, she sits at the intersection between biodiversity and cutting edge technology. With a PhD in herbal medicine, Odimegwu is a herbal medicine expert who got a grant from Gates Foundation to train African researchers on women’s health. According to her, women’s health has always been regulated because it’s complicated and what is complicating it is the hormones which can be up in the morning, down by afternoon. “It’s nature. It’s how we’re built, so it shouldn’t cause confusion. I didn’t know that other people were interested in the topic”, she told Vanguard. My area of research is biological patterns and I came across something very interesting. For many years they have been using broccoli to prevent certain gynecological cancers so as a researcher, I wanted to know what was in it. So, broccoli attacks inflammation and some people believe cancer is from inflammation”. Odimegwu wanted to be sure broccoli that is grown in Nigeria is the same as that broccoli. “My first degree was in Botany so I know about plants. I did some research. I got some in Jos, carried some down to Lagos and carried out the research to find out if broccoli’s Sulforaphane could modulate hormones in animals. The result I got was what I presented in Brazil. I used rabbits, dehydrated the broccoli powder in such a way as to optimise the Sulforaphane. If you feed the rabbit for 30 days, checking the estrogen throughout, we found that type of estrogen stable (there are other types) while the control was all over the place.” Clinical Studies Now, her team is preparing for the clinical human studies and all her high school friends have signed up to support her. “Essentially, there’s a solution in our food. item.title: How ISWAP’s southern expansion plot was foiled, commander killed in Ondo forest
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, also known as Anwar, a senior commander of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), alongside several of his fighters has brought major relief not only to the people of Ondo State but to the entire southern Nigeria. Ohida, who took over the coordination of ISWAP’s central and southern regional activities following the 2023 arrest of his superior, Abu Ikrimah (Abu Uwais) inside an Ondo forest, was killed during an intelligence-led operation deep inside the Owo Forest, Ondo State, early this month. Despite this breakthrough however, former Secretary to the Government of the Federation and now traditional ruler of Ilu-Abo in Akure North, Oba Olu Falae, has lamented that kidnapping and banditry still hold sway in rural communities The operation was executed by a combined team of Nigerian Army troops, operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), and officers of the Western Nigeria Security Network, codenamed Amotekun, with strategic intelligence backing from the United Kingdom. A major blow against southern expansion, security analysts have described the operation as another major counter-terrorism breakthrough by Nigerian security agencies, at a time authorities are intensifying efforts to prevent terrorist groups from extending their operational footprint from the North-East into the South. According to security sources, the forces carried out a thorough clearance operation in the forest, aimed at dislodging entrenched terrorist cells and preventing planned attacks on communities in southern Nigeria. Before the breakthrough, credible intelligence had indicated that Ohida was plotting to launch coordinated attacks on civilians during the festive period. The plot was designed to create a widespread atmosphere of insecurity that could undermine public confidence and disrupt preparations for the 2027 general elections. His elimination has therefore foiled the group’s plans to launch major terrorist attacks in parts of southern Nigeria during the coming festivities. The killing of Ohida came barely months after Nigerian and United States forces, in a joint counter-terrorism operation, killed another senior Islamic State commander, Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, in Borno State. For years, Ohida’s group had carried out several coordinated attacks against military formations, security installations and other soft targets as part of a deliberate strategy to establish or expand operational networks outside its traditional strongholds in northeastern Nigeria. The latest operation is being viewed by security authorities as a decisive attempt to disrupt ISWAP’s desperate push to establish a new operational corridor in the South. Trail of deadly attacks linked to Ohida Ohida was accused of involvement in several high-profile attacks on security formations across the country. item.title: 4 dead, many hospitalised in Benue after consuming herbal mixture
item.description: By Peter Duru Makurdi —No fewer than four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are battling for their lives in hospital after allegedly consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. It was gathered that the incident occurred after three men, identified as Magani, Mohamed and Kala, allegedly sold herbal preparations suspected to contain poisonous substances to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju township, last weekend. According to the eyewitness, “The development gained attention when some of those, who drank the mixture and their loved ones raised the alarm on November 2, 2026, after several residents, who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations started developing similar symptoms. “While the first victim reportedly died Tuesday morning, the second died in the early hours of Wednesday, and the third and fourth victims died later on November 4, 2026. “As we speak, over 14 other victims are currently battling for their lives, with many of them said to be in critical condition.” He disclosed that the three suspects allegedly involved in the sale of the herbal mixture were apprehended by the leadership of the Igede Youth Council, in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership, and subsequently handed over to the police in Oju. “We have been told that the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters has transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command, where the suspects are currently undergoing investigation,” he said. Speaking while handing over the suspects to the police, President of the Igede Youth Council, John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State government to ensure a thorough investigation of the incident and guarantee that justice was served. Ozzidi said the Igede youths had deliberately refrained from taking the law into their hands, resisting the temptation to subject the suspects to jungle justice. He explained that their decision to allow the law to take its course demonstrated their confidence in the state government to ensure justice is done in the matter. The youth leader also urged political officeholders from the area to follow up on the case to ensure that the deceased victims got justice and that the circumstances surrounding the suspected poisoning were fully established. Contacted, the Chairman of Oju council, Mr. Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he was yet to obtain the exact number of fatalities. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, Peter Aondongu, for comments were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to enquiries at press time. item.title: 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger Republic over Insecurity — UNHCR
item.description: *FG, UNHCR, Germany take essential services to hard-to-reach communities By Joseph Erunke & Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo NEARLY 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, UNHCR, has disclosed. This came the federal government, UNHCR and the German government launched a mobile service delivery initiative to address documentation challenges facing an estimated 3.7 million Nigerians displaced by conflict, insecurity and natural disasters. UNHCR, in a report monitored on Radio France International, RFI, Hausa Service, said about 327,500 Nigerians were already seeking refuge in Niger, which hosts over 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. Several hundred others have reportedly crossed into Benin Republic. UNHCR said most of the new arrivals settled in Diffa and Tahoua, with more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, arriving in Diffa since January. It warned that many displaced families were living in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean water and healthcare, amid rising cases of malnutrition and respiratory infections. The agency also said only about five per cent of Nigerians who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered, limiting their access to humanitarian assistance and essential services. It appealed for $11.4 million to support its response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin, including $2 million for urgent food, water, shelter, healthcare and protection needs. Meanwhile, the Federal Government, UNHCR and the German government have launched a mobile service delivery initiative to address documentation challenges facing an estimated 3.7 million Nigerians displaced by conflict, insecurity and natural disasters. Under the programme, 10 specially equipped mobile centres have been handed over to selected state governments to provide National Identification Numbers (NIN), birth certificates, Bank Verification Numbers, BVN, SIM registration, bank accounts and enrolment in the National Social Register. The initiative, tagged One Motor, Plenty Services, is designed to bring essential government services to internally displaced persons, refugees and vulnerable populations in remote communities. Speaking at the handover ceremony, the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro, said the intervention would address the exclusion of vulnerable citizens who could not access government services because of distance, displacement and lack of identification. “For millions of our citizens, the problem is not merely that services do not exist. The problem is that those services most often do not reach them,” the minister said. “They are invisible to the very system that has been designed to care for them. item.title: 2027 Polls: EU condemns rising violence, hate speech
item.description: *Says violence undermines democratic gains, hampers electoral process *Violence, rights suppression breed apathy, fear, distrust— NHRC *IPAC urges issues-based campaigns, flays hate speech By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The European Union, EU, yesterday expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Recall that in Katsina State recently, supporters of the All Progressives Congress, APC, travelling for a campaign flag-off in Funtua were reportedly attacked along the Yashi-Funtua route in October. A female passenger was injured, vehicles were damaged, and the police subsequently announced 14 arrests. Similarly, in Calabar, Cross River, the convoy of presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, came under attack on November 4, 2026. Police confirmed damage to vehicles and announced the arrest of a suspect, while investigations continued. He described open forums, free media, peaceful assembly and civil society organisations as essential to elections, noting that they promoted transparency and enabled citizens to share facts, debate and scrutinise candidates for elective office without fear of censorship or retaliation. “Free civic and political spaces also help hold leaders and institutions accountable by enabling CSOs and active citizens to monitor election administration, track campaign promises and challenge government policies. “By enabling free association and assembly, robust civic and political spaces prevent authorities from backsliding or from manipulating rules. “It is vital to ensure credibility and public confidence in an election. item.title: ACF crisis deepens
item.description: Moves to resolve the lingering supremacy battle within the ranks of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) have yet to produce results after a closed-door meeting by members of the Board of Trustees (BoT), the National Executive Committee (NEC) and some first-class emirs from the northern region ended in what some sources described as “deadlock.” Daily Trust learnt that the meeting, which took place on Tuesday at the private residence of the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, in Maitama, Abuja, lasted two hours between 5pm and 7pm without any tangible resolutions reached. The traditional rulers at the meeting included the Etsu Nupe, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar, and the Aku Uka of Wukari, Dr. Manu Ishaku Adda Ali. The Sultan was reportedly not at the meeting as he was attending to other matters of national importance somewhere. Although the details of the meeting, which was convened at the instance of the Sultan, were sketchy, sources privy to the happenings in the ACF confided in Daily Trust that the gathering focused on resolving the worsening division in the leadership of the northern socio-political group. One of the sources said both the Etsu Nupe and the Aku Uka expressed serious reservations over the inability of the BoT and NEC to arrive at a neutral ground and work together towards finding solution to the security and economic challenges afflicting the North. “In fact, one of the emirs alluded to the fact that the North is now a laughing stock…That we cannot speak with one voice at a critical moment of our existence,” he said. Our correspondents report that the meeting on Tuesday was a continuation of series of engagements with contending parties (NEC and BoT) towards resolving the protracted leadership crisis occasioned by alleged financial impropriety. Daily Trust learnt that the Sultan, with the support of the Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad and other northern traditional rulers have been having talks with the ACF leaders since the beginning of 2026 when the BoT and NEC engaged in blame game. On one hand, the Chairman of the BoT, Alhaji Bashir Dalhatu, with the support of some members, had asked the Secretary General of the organisation, Malam Murtala Aliyu, to leave. But Murtala had kicked saying his tenure will expire in December 2026. He reportedly has the support of some members, including the Chairman of the NEC, Barrister Mamman Mike Osuman, SAN. Besides the leadership tussle, the lodgement of about N3.9 billion donated to the ACP in a new account at JAIZ Bank, rather than in any of the main accounts of the organisation in First Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA) and Unity Bank, has caused disaffection among members. item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The growing cost of keeping factories operational in Nigeria is emerging as a major threat to industrial stability and employment, as employers struggle with rising electricity bills, multiple tax obligations, high borrowing costs and the uncertainties surrounding access to foreign exchange and essential production inputs. *AGM: Executive Secretary of the Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation (CANMPEF), Olorunfemi Oke; Trustee, S. I. Tella; President, Devakumar Edwin; First Vice-President, Rotimi Aluko; and Guest Speaker, Oscar Macaulay, at CANMPEF’s 46th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Lagos. For employers in the chemical and non-metallic products industries, the challenge extends beyond declining profit margins. The mounting cost of production is making business expansion, equipment modernisation and sustained investment increasingly difficult, raising concerns about the long-term capacity of companies to maintain existing operations and protect jobs. The situation has brought the question of job security into sharper focus, with manufacturers facing the difficult task of balancing rising operational expenses against the need to sustain production, meet financial obligations and maintain their workforce. The Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation, CANMPEF, in its Secretariat’s report by the Executive Secretary, Olorunfemi Oke at the 46th Annual General Meeting, AGM, in Lagos, identified high electricity costs, unreliable power supply, multiple taxation, expensive industrial finance and foreign-exchange difficulties as some of the major pressures confronting its members. The report painted a challenging picture of the operating environment for manufacturers, warning that the combination of these factors continued to affect production costs, operational efficiency, investment decisions and the competitiveness of locally manufactured products. On electricity, the Federation noted that the high cost of power and concerns about the reliability of supply had continued to place considerable pressure on manufacturing operations For energy-intensive industries, including chemical processing and the production of non-metallic products, electricity remains a critical production input that directly influences operational expenses, output and product pricing. The report observed that unreliable public electricity supply had increased manufacturers’ dependence on alternative power sources, adding another layer of financial pressure on businesses. It stated that the situation had disrupted production planning and increased operating expenses, with consequences for the competitiveness of locally manufactured goods. “Members reported that the high cost of electricity and concerns about the reliability of supply continued to place considerable pressure on manufacturing operations,” the report stated. item.title: Okeleji, Minister, calls for stronger link between education, jobs
item.description: By Juliet Umeh CEO of Seamless Technologies, Dr Emmanuel Okeleji, has called for stronger alignment between Nigeria’s education system and the skills businesses require, emphasising the importance of employer data in identifying workforce gaps and informing skills development. He made the call during a panel session titled: “Building Nigeria’s Future Workforce” at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, at the Transcorp Hilton, Abuja. Dr Okeleji joined the Honourable Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, Iyin Aboyeji and Dr Detoun Ogwo, Executive Director and Technical Advisor of the Skills Development Practice, to discuss how Nigeria can better prepare its workforce for changing labour market demands. Drawing on data from nearly 2,000 organisations across Africa that use Seamless Technologies’ platform, Dr Okeleji highlighted how recruitment and competency data can provide insight into the skills employers need and where gaps exist. The platform processes nearly 20 million job applications, giving the company visibility into hiring patterns, employer requirements and the competencies candidates bring to the recruitment process. “The Federal Government has put a lot of intention behind revising the education curriculum. The question now is how we can support the work that is already under way. “Seamless Technologies has a legitimate position to advise the government and provide the data we are seeing from employers that are hiring. This can help give a clearer picture of the skills businesses need and where the gaps exist,” he said. Dr Okeleji also highlighted the importance of small business survival in addressing unemployment, noting that creating jobs must go hand in hand with ensuring that the businesses providing those jobs can remain operational and grow over time. He stressed that smaller companies need the conditions and support to develop into sustainable businesses capable of providing long term employment. At a separate session convened by Sterling One Foundation, Dr Okeleji examined the growing mismatch between the skills job seekers possess and the competencies employers require. He observed that businesses continue to struggle to find qualified candidates, particularly for roles requiring specialised technical and practical skills. He further emphasised the responsibility of private sector organisations to contribute directly to reducing unemployment by expanding their workforce and creating more employment opportunities. “As a technology company, we have a responsibility to hire and contribute to reducing unemployment in Nigeria. The capital coming into the economy must translate into more jobs. There is still a lot of work to do, and I believe we can create more jobs,” Dr Okeleji added. The conversations at the summit highlighted the need for stronger collaboration between government, educational institutions and the private sector to address Nigeria’s workforce challenges. item.title: Gowon’s memoirs: Nigeria owes Awolowo an eternal debt, by Olu Fasan
item.description: Last week, I started a discussion of General Yakubu Gowon’s multi-themed memoirs, My Life of Duty & Allegiance. My focus was on the book’s general tone, which I find unduly self-justificatory. In his attempts to defend his legacy, General Gowon presents himself as a saintly figure who did no wrong as a leader, whereas some introspection and nuanced reflection would have helped. That said, the book is a treasure trove of insightful details that enrich our historical narrative. This week, I will focus on one of such insights, namely, the quality of governance and public service ethos under General Gowon’s regime, with Chief Obafemi Awolowo singled out as the arrowhead of a remarkable governance approach that, if replicated today, would transform how Nigeria is governed and, thus, this country’s fortunes. As a political economist and policy practitioner who spent nearly 20 years advising the UK government on diverse policy areas, in addition to teaching public policy, I have professional and intellectual interests in how government is run. Thus, I was enthralled by General Gowon’s fascinating accounts of how the affairs of state were conducted under his administration, with the triumvirate of politicians (as ministers), civil servants (as technocrats), and universities and think-tanks (as sounding boards) driving policy formulation and implementation and setting standards of good and effective governance. Sitting atop the triumvirate was Chief Awolowo, an extraordinarily transformative leader! Indeed, if General Gowon’s memoirs can be said to have a hero, that hero is Chief Obafemi Awolowo, appointed by Gowon as the Vice Chairman of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, and Commissioner of Finance in his administration. In every reference to Chief Awolowo in the memoirs, General Gowon writes glowingly and superlatively about him. Gowon also gives credit to his colleagues in the Supreme Military Council, SMC, and the first-class mandarins who ran the civil service for his administration’s successes, especially its ability to prosecute a 30-month civil war “without endangering the national economy”. But he reserves his most generous praise for Chief Awolowo. Hear Gowon: “Chief Awolowo’s business acumen, political sagacity, economic wizardry and thorough man-management ability would later prove quite useful and helpful in ensuring that we kept our finances intact during and immediately after the civil war that broke out a few weeks after his appointment to the FEC.” He adds: “Without any argument, he made invaluable contributions.” Of course, Chief Awolowo’s reputation preceded him. As the premier of the Western Region, he performed so superbly that Harold Wilson, then British prime minister, described him as a “world-class leader”, who would make an outstanding President of America or Prime Minister of Britain. item.title: Nigeria 2027 Election Watch: The Battle For The Ballot Deepens As Parties Lose Candidates, Gain Defectors And Confront The Courts
item.description: Nigeria’s 2027 election campaign is entering a phase in which the struggle for political influence is increasingly being accompanied by a struggle for legal recognition. Politicians are changing parties. Campaign organisations are being rearranged. Candidates are withdrawing from tickets. And the courts are being asked to determine who is entitled to contest. But another development is becoming difficult to ignore. Concerns about political violence, misinformation and the safety of electoral participation are growing as the campaign gathers momentum. The latest developments in Sokoto, Kano, Cross River and Ogun illustrate the different pressures confronting political parties. Meanwhile, the African Democratic Congress is fighting to preserve the legal validity of its national leadership and candidate nominations. Atiku’s supporters protesting in Abuja on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 And a new report from the National Peace Committee provides a troubling picture of the campaign environment. Taken together, these developments raise a question that goes beyond the usual calculations about party strength. Will Nigeria’s political parties enter the 2027 elections with settled candidates, functioning organisations and sufficient public confidence in the electoral process? That is today’s Political Signal. SOKOTO: THE DEFECTIONS CONTINUE In Sokoto State, the APC has received another group of defectors from the PDP and ADC. A Sokoto Government House statement issued on November 10 identified three PDP state executive officials, several local-government party chairmen and other political organisers among those who joined the ruling party. ADC ward officials and associated groups were also reported among the defectors. Some reports put the number of departing PDP local-government party chairmen at seven, although the published names clearly identify six. These are party officials, not elected local-government council chairmen. That distinction matters. The movement represents a change in the affiliations of local political organisers rather than a change in the composition of elected local councils. For the APC, the development adds politicians with experience in local party organisation. For the PDP and ADC, it raises questions about continuity in the affected ward and local-government structures. But there is a familiar qualification. A politician changing parties does not necessarily mean the voters who previously supported that politician will follow. That remains to be established through subsequent political activity and, ultimately, elections. KANO: ANOTHER CHANGE IN ADC’S ORGANISATION ADC is one of the opposition parties in Nigeria. X/@Aminuchindoo Kano has produced another development involving the ADC. A letter dated November 9 announced the appointment of a 14-member caretaker committee headed by Musa Ungogo. The committee is expected to serve for six months. The appointment comes against the background of earlier disagreements over the party’s
